utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we have the next witness, there is one matter I would like to announce, that is tomorrow we'll sit in the morning session instead of the afternoon, since the Brdjanin case is over. So this courtroom is free in the morning. Another matter is that we reserved the courtroom tomorrow afternoon for a Status Conference, which is not long. I believe it's about 30 to 40 minutes. The subject matter of this meeting is to continue the discussion of the 65 ter filings by Mr. Blagojevic's Defence. But if we could finish tomorrow's witness earlier, if we still have time in the morning session, we'll simply turn into that Status Conference in the morning so that we could have much more time in the afternoon to enjoy the sun, if there's any. Well, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready for your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am, Mr. President. No protective measures have been requested. And for tomorrow's witness, there will be none either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could please tell us what your name is.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Jovan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: N-i-k-o-l-i-c.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And do you have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Jole.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Nikolic, where are you from?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: From Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And where is Kravica?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is that where you were -- is that where you grew up?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, do you know Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you know him when you were growing up?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you did not attend school together?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where did you attend school, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I completed elementary school in the village of Kravica, then I went to the secondary school for teachers in Tuzla. I completed that school, and then I attended the pedagogical academy in Sabac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Prior to the war, what was your occupation?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I was a teacher at the elementary school Petar Kocic in Kravica. And I was also a teaching expert at that school. Then I served as principal for two terms. And just before the war, I was president of the municipal conference of the Socialist Alliance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this school that you were the principal of and where you taught, was that a multi-ethnic school?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was a multi-ethnic school, a school which covered four branches of schools, two of them were Muslim ones -- or rather Muslim children attended those schools. And then from grade 5 to grade 8, these children attended school in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know the numerical or percentage breakdown between Serb children and Muslim children?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In the early period, when I just started working as school principal, the ratio was approximately 50:50 per cent. And just before the war broke out, it changed to two-thirds of Muslim children to one-third of Serb children.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What do you today?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Today I'm principal of Branko Radicevic elementary school in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And do you have Muslim children or Bosniaks attending?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Muslim children also attend that school. Those are the children of the returnees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to focus your attention to July 1995. Okay. If you could please tell us what was your occupation during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In 1995 I was director of the co-op in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what this co-op was all about. What did it do? Who belonged to it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The co-op had three work units within it, so together they formed what we called complex co-op. Those were the co-ops in Fakovici, Bratunac, and Kravica. The main activity of those co-ops were production of agricultural produce, sale of them, then we also had a bakery which provided bread for the citizens of Bratunac municipality. Cooperation was one of the main features of this co-op, which meant that the residents of the area cooperated in order to produce this produce. So first they produced them and then they sold what they did not need. The complex co-op, where I worked as a director, was the one which coordinated all of those activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Approximately how many people or families participated in this co-op?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The co-op itself had 25 to 30 employees, whereas these branch offices that I told you about, each of those co-ops covered about 2 to 250 households.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, during this period of time, were you also mobilised in the army?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us why not.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In December of 1992 during the Muslim attack on the village of Kravica, where I was at the time, I was gravely injured, wounded. Following my treatment, I became unfit for military service. I was declared as such, therefore the army wasn't interested in me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So when, approximately if you could give us the month, when did you stop being in the army?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: As I've told you, I was wounded on the 24th of December. I was treated in Zvornik until the 11th of January. And after that, I continued receiving treatment at the military medical academy in Belgrade until the 10th of March. I spent the entire 1993 receiving treatment in Banja Koviljaca, which is a spa. I was declared to be unfit for military service on the 20th of May, 1994, by the decision of a military commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Incidentally, in the co-op that you were managing, were there individuals working for the co-op that were doing their working obligation?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And just briefly, if you could remind us what that is.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The men who were unfit for military service were the ones who worked in co-ops. In addition to that, there were some women who also worked in order to contribute to the further functioning of the co-op.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to direct your attention to the day when Srebrenica fell, if you could use that as a point of reference, that date being 11 July 1995. Do you recall, sir, what you were doing on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In July and second half of June, our co-ops started an organised campaign to buy off the entire harvest of berries, raspberries. A lot of raspberries are grown in our region, and many people are engaged in harvesting raspberries. This is how it was that year as well. So on the 11th and before the 11th, I was at the co-op where we were harvesting raspberries, which had to be picked and then transported to refrigerated warehouses in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So -- if I understand you correctly, traditionally the July month is raspberry month for the co-op. And you were busily engaged with the raspberry season?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you -- let me focus you on the next day, the day after Srebrenica fell, that would be the 12th of July, 1995. Do you recall what you did that day?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The 12th of July is a holiday in my village. This is the day when the church in Kravica celebrates the day of its patron saint. Regardless of the situation that existed at the time, we were in Kravica on that day -- or rather, I was in Kravica attending the church service. And following that, I went to the house, which is 500 metres from the church -- or rather, the remains of the house which was burnt during war operations in 1993. I stayed there until afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me stop you here. When you say "the house," whose house was that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That was the house of my parents, my brother, and me. It was our family house in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And just incidentally, at that period in time were you living in that house or were you living elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I was living in town. I had an apartment owned by myself, my wife, and my children. We lived in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So when you went to this house, to your house, your family house in Kravica on 12 July 1995, was there anyone else there during the --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- celebration?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I went there together with Marko Tomic. There were few people attending the church service, in view of what was going on. We stayed there some time, then we continued on to my house and came back in the afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Was your -- were your parents alive at that period of time?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: My mother had died earlier. My father lives in Sabac, but he came to Bratunac on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Was he there at the house during this Slava celebration, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you remain there the entire day, or did you leave at some point?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I stayed there until the afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then where did you go?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Then I returned to Bratunac. And together with a friend who drove me, I went to the warehouse of the agricultural co-op, which is approximately halfway between Bratunac and Ljubovija. I went there to see what was going on and to see whether everything that we had planned was unfolding well under supervision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you notice anything unusual at that time, July 12th, 1995, that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Upon our return from Kravica, we saw that the traffic was more active. We saw buses travelling from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje -- or rather, to Zvornik and I don't know where else they could have gone, to Kladanj and on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you notice by any chance who were in those buses?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There were people in the buses. I didn't know who they were. We assumed that that was the evacuation or the departure of Muslims from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you went -- from there -- after visiting -- when you went to the agricultural warehouse, if I understand your testimony correct, did you notice anything unusual there at that time?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. But this is the warehouse in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There was nothing unusual going on there at that warehouse. Everything was as usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. I misunderstood you. I thought this was the Kravica agricultural warehouse. Now, when you got into Bratunac --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you tell us -- when you went to Bratunac. When you physically went there, did you do anything that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: As I've told you, I went to the warehouse, I stayed there for some time. I think that on that day I was invited to attend a meeting which took place in the SDS premises. I was asked to attend the meeting, scheduled by Miroslav Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did you attend the meeting?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall who else attended the meeting, just some of the people?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Those were mostly people who were in town who were not engaged in the military. Among others I remember that Aco Tesic was there, Ljupko Ilic. I'm not sure about Ljubo Simic, whether he was there. And then also a number of other people who happened to be there in the area, in town, where they were available to attend the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, how long did this meeting last, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The meeting was organised in two parts. During the first session, Mr. Deronjic told us that pursuant to the decision of the president of the state, he was appointed civilian commissioner, as that post was known as the time. And that following the completion of these operations, there would be an organised revitalisation of the territory of Bratunac and Srebrenica, that there will be a lot of work for civilian officials and for residents as well. The second session of the meeting took place in the SDS offices, and I did not attend that part of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall whether there was a -- whether Mr. Deronjic had been informed that he was wanted on the telephone?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was called to the telephone, and a group of people accompanied him. I didn't want to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So I take it you don't know what transpired during that telephone conversation?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. After that meeting, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Following the meeting, I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. On your way to the house did you notice whether there were any buses or trucks or -- with men in them?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And where -- do you recall where you would have noticed those buses or trucks?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I drove in my car to the apartment. This was in the part of the road which goes on to Konjevic Polje. So near the intersection towards Konjevic Polje and Kravica. This is where the buses were. There were some trucks as well with tarpaulin, and I couldn't see whether anybody was there on the trucks. I couldn't see what was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. In Bratunac town do you recall seeing, in the grad, do you recall seeing any buses or trucks that particular night? We're talking about July 12th, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now. You indicated that you went home. Did you go out again that night?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The next day --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The next day I went to work, because as I've told you we had a lot of work involving the harvesting of raspberries. So I went to my office to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where is your office located?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The office of the co-op is at the intersection of the road leading to Srebrenica and the road coming in from Ljubovija. To be more precise, it is in the very centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you walk to your office or did you drive to your office?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I walked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, as you were walking towards your office, did you see anyone?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. When you got to your office, your office building, did you encounter anyone?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When I came to my office building, there were workers there with whom I had worked. There were no other people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, did you notice anyone familiar or did anyone familiar come up to you at some point in time?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In the office?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Not in the office, outside.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you notice Momir Nikolic on that particular morning?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Momir Nikolic a little later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. About what time?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I can say it was around 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. What time did you go to your office?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In the morning, at 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Where was it when you -- where were you when you saw Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I had left my office, and I was observing the buses and trucks moving from the direction of Srebrenica. And then Momir Nikolic came along.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And was he in a car? Was he on foot, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Momir was in a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall the make of the car and colour of the car by any chance?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It was blue and it was a Fiat Zastava.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you know Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Oh, for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And what were your relations with him at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mostly official, not especially close, but there were no problems between us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you saw Momir Nikolic, did he say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. He offered to take me to Potocari so that I could see what was going on there, in view of the fact that the evacuation was underway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you accept his offer?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I got into the car, and then he suggested that I go home and change into a uniform, which I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, if you hadn't been mobilised, since you had been injured I believe it was December 1992, how is it that you would have a uniform at home?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I had a uniform I had kept. And secondly, my brother was in the army, so there happened to be a uniform in my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And did you change into a uniform?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And after that, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After that we got into the car again and set out toward Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. On the way to Potocari, did you see anyone that you were acquainted with?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. In front of the administration building where I had met Momir, there were two friends of ours. Perica Vasovic and Stojan Ilic, also known as Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And what happened when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They stopped us. Momir stopped the car, and he took the two of them to Potocari as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So now all four of you are in the car. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How long of a drive is it from the point where all four of you are in a car to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, it's a 10-minute drive at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: During that 10-minute drive, did Momir Nikolic tell you what his functions were?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Was there any conversation at all, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, he said that what was happening in Srebrenica was finished now, that the civilians, the women, men, children were surrendering, that they were coming down to Potocari, and that they were now being evacuated and transported toward Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you got to Potocari, could you please describe to us what you did.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: As I've already said, I went to Potocari at the invitation of Momir Nikolic, out of pure personal curiosity. Because things were happening up there, it was nearby, and there was nothing to prevent me from going to see what was happening. We arrived at the checkpoint, that is an area where there are a number of old factories within a compound. We stopped there, got out of the car, and we saw that at this site there were many women, children, elderly people, as well as men who happened to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. What did you do in particular?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't do anything. I did nothing at all. I recognised some people; they said hello. I replied. And I was horrified to see the suffering of the people there, the women, the children, the people fleeing who had come there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about Momir Nikolic? Did you notice what he was doing?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: He didn't do anything special. He was there, just like me. He saw some people he knew and said hello to them. So we stayed there for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you ever see Momir Nikolic go up to any commanders, unit commanders, to give instructions or to coordinate?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did Momir Nikolic ever tell you that he had been appointed by the Main Staff to be the coordinator of all those units that were located in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That's been quite a number of leading questions up until now in crucial things with Momir Nikolic. And here just a moment ago he asked him whether Momir Nikolic told him what his function was and the witness said no. And now he went on and asked the same, in fact, leading question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may respond, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm perfectly -- first of all, I'm entitled to see whether Momir Nikolic informed him that he had been a coordinator or the coordinator by the Main Staff. You know. It does call for yes or no, but also I believe it's vital information in light of Momir Nikolic's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could simplify your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did Momir Nikolic ever inform you of any functions that had been given to him by the Main Staff in respect to --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- with respect to the evacuation process?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you know Momir Nikolic quite well, do you know not?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What kind of person is Momir Nikolic? Please describe him, his character, so we can understand with whom we are dealing with.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, it's a thankless task, evaluating a person like that. But as far as I know him he's an ambitious man, overambitious, I could even say arrogant, and above all, a very bold man. He grew up in the same community that I did, but he didn't have any close friends. And this was because of the way he behaved toward people he worked with. People like him are not easily accepted in the community. And Momir Nikolic chose that lifestyle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Had Momir Nikolic been appointed to an important position, based on your understanding of his character, do you believe, or do you know whether he would have at least informed you of the important position that he had been given --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's purely speculative. And he's certainly not a psychologist here testifying what a person of a certain character would answer to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's quite a speculative question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, I'll rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope you drop it. I think you have driven the nail into the place already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may be permitted one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is Momir Nikolic a boastful person, someone who would boast about himself, his importance?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. How long did you stay in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We stayed in Potocari for some 20 or 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And during that 20 or 30 minutes, you said that -- you said hello to some people. Were they soldiers? Were they Muslims? Were they both? Would you please tell us.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: As I've already said, I was seen there by some Muslims I knew. We said hello, and that's the end of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, after you -- when you left, how did you -- where did you go?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: On our way -- or rather, when we returned, we arrived at the administration building where I had met Momir. We said goodbye. And he went off, saying he was going to the brigade headquarters. And I went to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you do anything else that day, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After being in the office, I went again to the cooperative warehouse in Bratunac and I stayed there for three or four hours. After that, I returned home again. This was my working day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you returned home, did you happen to notice if there were any buses with Muslim males in them?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I went home by car, and along the way I saw buses full of Muslims leaving Srebrenica and moving in the direction of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you go out that night, once you got home?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The next morning - this is now the 14th of July - do you recall that particular day?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how it began and when.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In the morning I got up. I went to the headquarters of the cooperative, and we looked at the reports from the sales points to see how the raspberries were selling. We did that every morning for the previous day. We established the quantities that had been sold, and we had some coffee. We drew up a plan for that day. And after that, I went to Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And about what time would it have been when you went to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I went to Kravica at around 9.30 or maybe 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And was there a particular reason for going to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was a reason. We had not received the way bills, the receipts, from the sales point in Kravica, nor had we received a report from the people in charge of selling the raspberries. Together with Dragan Nikolic, who was to take over the management of the plant in Kravica, I went to Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you got there did you notice anything?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. When I arrived at the cooperative compound which had an administration building and other buildings, such as, for example, a barn for cattle, warehouses, a mixed goods shop, and a place where we prepared cattle feed, I went to the administration building. We stopped the car, and then we started off toward the warehouse, where we noticed a certain number of people. And we noticed that in that part of the warehouse, ugly things were happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to stop you here, and I want to go step by step as to exactly what you saw. Would you please tell us, when you say "ugly things," what are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: First of all, I had not expected to come across such a scene in this warehouse, which consists of two parts. There were a lot of corpses there. At the other end, near the other end of the warehouse, I noticed that shooting was still going on and that people were being liquidated. They were being brought to the warehouse and then shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you watch anyone get shot?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw that, and I reacted. I couldn't stand it. And I started yelling and cursing, asking why they were doing this. And then I myself was in danger from that group of men who were doing the execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me stop you here. Tell us exactly what you saw. How were these executions occurring?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, a long time has elapsed since then, so it's hard to say, of course, but the people were lined up, told to lie down. After that, they said they had to be vaccinated and that the vaccination had to be checked. And then --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me stop you. Let me stop you. I want you to describe to us what they mean by vaccination and what you mean by the vaccination having to be checked. We're going to go step by step.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There were lines of five or six men who were told to lie down. And then the man in charge said that to be vaccinated, and this was done by shooting them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And then the order was issued to check or verify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. When the initial shooting took place, the vaccination as they called it, where were they shooting -- where were they shooting these individuals?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: In the back of the head.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when the next person had to recheck the vaccination, where were --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Under the left shoulder blade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, you said when you saw that you reacted. First of all, could you please describe to us whether you recognised these individuals.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you describe --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't know them, nor could I guess afterwards who these people had been. It's a fact that what I saw is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me stop you. Did you recognise any of the men from being -- from the Bratunac area?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: As I've already said, I didn't recognise any of the men carrying out the execution. And I am convinced that there were no men among them from the brigade, that is the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to get to that. But first, were you able to see the faces of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They had uniforms and they wore masks over their faces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So I take it you could not see their face?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you able to recognise their voices?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that you thought that they were not from the Bratunac Brigade. Could you please explain to us how is it that you think they could not have been from the Bratunac Brigade if their faces were covered up.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I can assert, because before I was wounded I used to belong to the Bratunac Brigade. I was deputy commander of the Kravica Battalion. And I had other duties. For example, I was the president of the municipal veterans' association, and the members of the brigade knew me well. So that there wouldn't have been the incident that happened, had these men been the members of the brigade we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you say "the incident," what incident are you speaking about?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I am speaking about what happened when I approached and saw the dead men in the warehouse. When I saw people being shot I reacted. I saw and I started yelling, saying: "Why are you killing these people? Why are you doing this?" Then they started coming towards me with their guns pointed at me, intending to kill me, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what happened?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After this, a group of men intervened who had been observing this, because there were houses across the road from the cooperative. So they intervened and tried to convince those men that I was the managing director of the cooperative, that I had been previously the deputy commander of a battalion, and they barely managed to save my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you recognise any of the men that helped you in saving your life?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was people from Kravica, elderly people. For example, Sveto Milanovic, Velizar Vasic, Zoran Eric, and Perica Vasovic was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. After that incident, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After this, after this incident, I quickly went to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And where did you go once you got to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When I arrived in Bratunac, I went to the Municipal Assembly building, that is to the Executive Board offices. And I informed the civilian authorities that in Kravica, in the warehouse, there was chaos and that there were many dead men. And I told them about all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And what were you expecting them to do?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The reason I went there was for them to take appropriate measures, that is to carry out asanacija or sanitisation of the terrain and to take those measures they were authorised to take.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you expect them to stop the killings or to try to stop the killings?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. I can say that the killing was nearly over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Was man number one of Bratunac there?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I went to Srbislav Davidovic's office, Ljubo Simic was there too, and Deronjic came in later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you contact the Bratunac Brigade to see if they could intervene?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't contact the Bratunac Brigade, nor do I think that I had either reason to do so or an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you ever find out where those individuals were, where they were from, the ones that were committing those executions?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, after this incident, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: After that, I stayed talking to the representatives of civilian authorities and then received a promise from them that they would take appropriate measures and that they would get civilian protection involved and the company which at the time performed the duties of sanitisation or the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you ever return to the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I went back there. As I've told you, we had cattle there and we had the production going on. There were some of our people there, and also I was personally interested in ensuring that things started functioning there again. And I thought that my being there would help it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were the executions still going on when you got back there?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When I came back, the people who had been there were gone and there were no more executions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. How long did the clean-up take place of the Kravica warehouse, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The clean-up of the warehouse lasted from Friday afternoon through Saturday and Sunday. I think it was completed around 1600 hours on the 16th, on Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How can you be so precise? 1600 hours, 16th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I can because there was an unpleasant event that took place on the 16th of July. When I returned from Kravica, I was told that my brother had been killed, who had been at the front line in Zvornik area. This is why I know the exact time and date, because upon receiving that news I had to take care of the funeral for my brother and consoling his family and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you know what happened to the bodies that were at the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The bodies that were at the Kravica warehouse were buried in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you actually see the burial process?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. I did not leave Kravica. However, the grave was located near the road and one could see it when travelling on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you said that the 16th of July is a memorable day because of the loss of your brother. Do you recall whether on that day the burying process or the digging process in Glogova was ongoing, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That was on Saturday and Sunday. The 16th was Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you -- so was it still going on on Sunday, the 16th?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And I've told you, we left Kravica, and this was completed at around 1600 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. What about the next day, the 17th. Did you notice whether - in Glogova now, not in Kravica - whether the equipment was there and the burying process was continuing, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I wasn't there on the 17th. I was in Zvornik on the 17th. As I've told you, I went to receive my brother's body so that we could bury him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you gave a statement to the Prosecutors back in 2001, I believe it was November 28, 2001. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you were given an opportunity to look at your statement. Right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And initially you noted that part of your statement or part of the information that you had given the Office of the Prosecution in Banja Luka was not in your statement?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: A certain portion was missing. Right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then I believe it was yesterday that I gave you the opportunity to listen to the tape that was provided to us, and then you were able to hear the rest of that portion that for some reason there was a mix-up, hadn't been translated and transcribed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: After listening to that tape, I can only assume that you were confident that that tape contained everything that you had said to the Prosecutors in Banja Luka on 28 November 2001. Right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you listened to that tape which contained your entire statement to them, you did not state anything in that -- during that questioning process anything about Momir Nikolic and the trip to Potocari on the 13th of July, 1995. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us why is it, if you know, why is it that you did not tell the Prosecutors back on the 28th November, 2001, why you didn't tell them anything about your encounter with Momir Nikolic, his suggestion that you go and put on a uniform, picking up a couple of other people, driving off to Potocari, and watching or observing Nikolic walking around more or less in the same fashion as you did? Would you please tell us why you didn't tell that to the Prosecutors back in Banja Luka on 2001.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, when I was asked by the Prosecution to speak about the events in Srebrenica in the summer of 1995, I went to that interview with great pleasure, because I wanted to state what I knew, and thus enable the Prosecution to uncover the truth regarding those events. As to the circumstances that you just asked me about, Bratunac is a small town and all of us know each other well there. There were some people who contacted me when I went to testify, and they asked me not to mention them there, due to the unpleasant consequences that they could expect as a result of that. Some of the people who asked me that and even insisted on me not mentioning their names, Momir Nikolic was among them. The investigators from the OTP who questioned me did not insist on that at all. They asked me whether I was there and with whom. I mentioned Stojan Ilic. They didn't ask me about Momir, so I didn't say anything about that. And I would like to apologise to the Prosecution for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, incidentally, did Vidoje Blagojevic ever contact you, like Momir Nikolic, insisting that you not mention his name in any way?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, as I understand it, you also gave a statement to the RS police.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I believe in that statement there -- you don't mention Momir Nikolic again?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They didn't ask me about Momir either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, at some point - recently I would suspect - you were contacted, were you not, by the lawyers of Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And as I understand it, they were probably interested in getting some information from you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you give them a statement?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, this trip to Potocari that you told us about under oath, do you recall whether you told them the same story?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I told them the same story, too. And I've repeated it just now here, and that is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you just tell them or did they record it, write it down, make a statement, have you sign it, have it available in the event they wanted to use it in court?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They took information and the statement from me. There was also some mention of me testifying here before this court. Following the events surrounding Momir Nikolic, they didn't contact me again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it one of the things they wanted to have you highlight was this trip to Potocari where you all walking around like sightseers in Potocari on July 13 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then you were never contacted again?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Following that, I had no more contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe I am through, but again, since we're just about up for our break, if I could have the indulgence of sort of running through -- do an accounting to make sure I haven't missed a point. I believe I'm through. I just want to be absolutely certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll take a break, and we'll resume at 15 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe I just have a couple more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, in the part of the statement that was missing that you gave to the Prosecutor's office back in 2001, what portion of your statement was missing? What events?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The part that was missing was the part of the statement which pertains to my arrival in Kravica and my stay there, as well as the incident that I described to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your reaction to seeing the killings and trying to intervene?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I noted to you before coming here today that we had been provided with some information from Muslim witnesses stating that you were in Potocari not on the 13th, as you noted, but on the 12th. Do you recall me bringing that to your attention?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are you certain that you were not there on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I am certain that I went to Potocari on the 13th and that on the 12th, I was in Kravica at the church. Therefore, on the 13th I was in Potocari; on the 14th and 15th I was in Kravica; and then on the 16th, on Sunday, after that all that was finished, I heard about the tragedy in my family. So all of these dates fully correspond with my chronology of time and I am fully certain of these dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just so I understand you correctly, you're using July 12th, which is St. Peter's Day as your focal point as to where you were that day and the following day. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I take it if you had been to Potocari on the 12th of July, 1995, would you readily admit to that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Why not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you do anything to anyone in Potocari during the time that you were there that you would worry about here today as you testify?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you harm anyone?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you threaten anyone?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. I have no further questions. Mr. Stojanovic may have some questions, who is representing Mr. Jokic. The Prosecutor, I'm sure, will have some questions, as perhaps the Judges. I would appreciate it if you would be as frank and as complete with your answers as you have been with me. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, good afternoon. Good afternoon to the witness as well. We have no questions for this witness, in view of his testimony today and the contents of the indictment against our client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination? Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, there will be a few issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me go over a few areas which you have discussed with Mr. Karnavas. Now, I take it that you repeated several times you weren't in Potocari on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So you wouldn't have seen Momir Nikolic acting or not acting or whatever he was doing in Potocari on that day?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I went with Momir on the 13th to Potocari, as I've stated today. I went there because I was asked by him and out of my personal curiosity. That's why I went with Momir to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Waespi, I don't think the witness understands your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. I'll just ask it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Because you were not in Potocari on the 12th, you don't know what Momir Nikolic was doing in Potocari on the 12th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, let's go to the 13th when you were in Potocari, as you testified today. What time in the day did you meet up with Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It was 10.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And I believe you were in the office a couple of hours prior to that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you hadn't met Momir Nikolic before you met him just prior to going to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So you don't know what he was doing on that morning before the two of you met?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go into Potocari. I believe you talked to the -- told the investigators when you met with them in Banja Luka a little bit, you know, how far you went in Potocari. And today I believe you told us you went past these old factories. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you also mentioned the checkpoint which you passed?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, how far into the compound or into the road towards Srebrenica did you actually go?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. The gentleman never said that he went into Srebrenica. And the checkpoint as I understand it is before you get to Potocari. It's the yellow bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could ask some more questions to lay some foundations on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I will certainly do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The checkpoint you mentioned, I don't think you clarified where that checkpoint was located. Can you do that for us.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The checkpoint was at the yellow bridge, which is halfway on the road between Bratunac and Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Okay. And then you went towards Potocari, these old factories. Now, tell us how far did you go into that scene which you described today.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: We stopped at the entrance to the factory. These factories that I've mentioned today were full of people. We didn't go in deep. We didn't go and mix with the people. We stayed on the side, on the edge, just before this tremendous amount of people who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: How far away from this tremendous amount of people did you stay -- did you stop?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: At the very entrance, in front of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Close enough so some people could recognise you?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Did you also see buses and trucks alongside that road?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Did you see any men over there? I believe you testified that you saw women, children, elderly. And then I quote you: "As well as men who happened to be there." Do you remember -- what did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I said that there were people of various age there, women, children, adults, the elderly, men of these -- of this age. So people of various age. Women, children, men, the elderly, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Did you see elderly -- did you see men of able age, military-able age there being grouped together?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: They were there, too. They were not separated from the rest of the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So they were together in that crowd, which you have described earlier?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me show you a brief clip of that area, and let me ask you whether you recognise the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And I believe, Your Honour, it's Prosecution Exhibit 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that the clip is from the 13th at around 10.00 or 11.00 in Potocari, because that's when the gentleman was there, as opposed to the 12th. So I just want to make sure that we're not getting into some misleading territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The gentleman --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think so long as the clip is from the 13th, we'll be all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, we want it to be relatively to the time and place when he was there. If it was 13th at night, of course we don't want that. 13th in the morning -- so if I can have some representations here on the record that that is so, then I will sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, everybody in this courtroom knows this clip. It's the clip showing the white house with the people detained. And we know that it's from the 13th. And if the witness says he hasn't seen that scenery, then that's fair enough, then we can move on. But I think it's absolutely proper to show this witness who claims to have been there, to show him that clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As long as he -- I'm told by the Prosecutor that it's the 13th, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If the lights could be dimmed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you remember having seen this house to -- with the people crammed together on the balcony? Do you remember that when you were there?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You also saw a few people there in uniforms. Have you recognised anybody you knew?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't recognise anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, I believe in your statement to the investigators, you told them that you saw the president of the municipality in Bratunac, Mr. Simic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know whether Mr. Simic was there on that day only or whether he was on the second -- on another day as well? Do you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, I don't. I only saw him briefly. I passed by him and went back. I have no information as to how long he stayed there. I have heard about some statements to the effect that President Simic was duty-bound to bring a tank truck filled with water there and bring medical assistance, and that that was what his activities there were about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you are absolutely certain that you saw him on that day, on the 12th of July -- I'm sorry, on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, during that time you spent together with Momir Nikolic sightseeing - but I believe that's a word from Mr. Karnavas - together, for how long were you there?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I've already said, we were there for about 20 minutes observing what was going on there. Bearing in mind what we saw, I insisted on going back and Momir agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you said that you approached this group of people and you talked to some of these civilians. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I recognised a forester from Bjecava. He said hello to me, I greeted him. I saw some other people. And it all boiled down to brief conversations about how they were or what they thought would happen. But I was unable to give them any information about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Was Momir Nikolic with you when you talked to this forester?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He was with me and he said hello, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: For this period of time, was Momir Nikolic with you all the time or did he have other whereabouts?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't go off anywhere. We were together the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: How far together were you? 2 metres?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, we were right next to each other, right next to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: For 20 minutes?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So every person you met, he had met as well?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And every person he talked to, you would be aware of as well?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Not every person.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you know a person called Dusko Jevic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, I believe you -- I asked you already about these men which we have seen on the clip. And I'm not sure whether you answered the question, but did you see separations between the women, children, elderly on the one side, and the men on the other side?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: While I was there, I didn't see anyone being separated off. I didn't see men being separated off from the women and children. I just saw a crowd of people, and they were all mixed with respect to age and generation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Okay. Let me move on to the next day at Kravica. Now, I believe you were in Kravica on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And also on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: On the 12th, I was in my family home. On the 14th, I went to the agricultural co-op. On the 12th, I didn't go there because it was a holiday and the co-op where these buildings are is below the road that I used to go to my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And on the 13th, I take it you were not in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you about Kravica, the 14th. You are a native of Kravica, are you not?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And in fact you are a teacher, even the principal, of the Kravica school there?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So you know where the school in Kravica is?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Of course I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, on the 14th when you were there, were you made aware by anybody about the presence of Muslim men who were being detained on buses and trucks parked in front of the school building?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the -- before he answers that question, when he was there. The previous question was: Does he know where the school is? The next question is: When you were there, the implication being or the suggestion that he was at the Kravica school the day before. So I would like a clear question, in light of the language differences. If he was at the school, and if so that question can be asked. But the way it's phrased, I'm afraid it's somewhat confusing. And perhaps, if I could assist my colleague, if he could ask some questions how far is the school from the agricultural centre, that way we can all have our bearings for some of us who haven't been there, me not being one of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Waespi, maybe you could ask more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You testified you were at the church in Kravica on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you also told us that you had some land in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, in relation to the school in Kravica, how far away is your land?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: My land and my family home are 2 kilometres and 300 metres away from the school in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And the school in Kravica, how far away from the road between Bratunac and Konjevic Polje is that school?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The road going from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje passes right by the Oka co-op. And the school is about 200 or 300 metres away from the road, to the side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Okay. And to the side, meaning towards the village which is north of the road or south of the road?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Parallel to the road, on the right-hand side is the school. And it's about 300 metres away from the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And how far away from the co-op, the actual Kravica warehouse, is the school?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The school is about 500 metres away from the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, we've heard that you were there during those days after the fall of Srebrenica a substantial amount of time in Kravica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I spent time in Kravica, as I said, on the 14th, the 15th, and the 16th. That was three days. But I did go home to Bratunac to sleep at home, and I would go back to Kravica in the morning. This was the period I mentioned just a while ago when the civilian protection forces were carrying out the asanacija, the sanitisation, of the terrain and of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now -- and you were there in Kravica also on the 12th, as we have heard?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Well, if I'm to be quite precise, I have to say that on the 12th I was in the village of Bacici, which belongs to Kravica. On the 12th, I passed through Kravica and went to my hamlet, spent the day there, and went back to Bratunac. On the 12th, I didn't spend time in Kravica, as such. I wasn't actually in Kravica; I was in a small hamlet about 2 kilometres away from Kravica. And the name of this hamlet is Bacici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you also know many people in Kravica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Okay. Now, going back to my original question, in all these times you were in Kravica during those days, and even later, have you heard that Muslim men were being detained in the school in Kravica during these days, between the 12th and the 15th?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just for the record, I just want to make sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think the question should have been whether, whether. We haven't had any live witnesses, viva voce witnesses, come in here and say that. So I understand there is a statement from one witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: That's simply not correct, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think in cross-examination the Prosecution could ask these kind of questions. There's no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, if my memory serves me correct - and perhaps I'm a little tired - I don't recall a witness coming in here saying that there were prisoners in the Kravica school. I could be wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: It's Witness 135, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I withdraw the objection, and I apologise for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me ask you whether you know where the supermarket is in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I ask you the same question: Are you aware of the detention of Muslim men on buses and trucks parked in front or near the supermarket in any of those days?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, on this one I'm going to object. This is the one, and I confused them. On this one we don't have any viva voce witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's not a reason for objecting to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The way the question is phrased is if we're talking about a fact. I will concede the point on the earlier one with respect to the schools. But with respect to buses, as I understand it, we haven't heard any viva voce witnesses who will be subject to cross-examination and confrontation. So that's why I'm objecting. If the question was posed as whether, whether there were as opposed to that there were, one being the possibility that they were there versus the fact that they were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, there's some nuances in this question, but I don't think it's a great deal. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just for the record it's Witness 112, indeed, a 92 bis witness, but I don't see the relevance in terms of evidentiary value in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, if you could please ask -- answer the question, witness. Did you hear, are you aware, of the presence of detained people near the supermarket in Kravica these days?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that. I didn't hear about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Did you hear any gunfire while you were there in Kravica on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: On the 14th did you go into Kravica itself, the village of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: On the 14th I went from Bratunac to the premises of the co-op. I didn't enter the village; I went directly to the co-op, which is about 500 metres away from the centre of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: How far away from the road is the supermarket?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: It's right by the road, by the roadside.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: When you came on the 14th, did you see any buses or trucks being parked outside the supermarket?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. There weren't any.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Going back to or staying on this topic on the 14th in Kravica, now, was there anybody you knew in Kravica that morning? And you may have to repeat the names which you have given to us.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: When I arrived in the compound of the co-op, I was with Dragan Nikolic. We entered the co-op compound. On the left-hand side where the warehouses are, we saw the scene I described a short while ago. And because it's very upsetting for me, I wouldn't like to repeat it. When I entered the co-op compound, on the other side where there are a few houses, five or six elderly villagers came in and started going toward the buildings in the coop. These are elderly people who lived there, Sveto Milanovic, Slavorad Vasic, Savo Redjenovic [phoen], Perica Vasovic, and also the guards who were employed by the co-op, Vuko Markovic, Zoran Eric, Milos Cvjetinovic. These are the people who were there when I entered the co-op compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, did you see Krsto Simic among these people?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. Krsto Simic arrived on the following day. He was recruited to do that work, and I saw him on the following day, not on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what was he doing on the following day?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Operating the loading and transport machinery.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what kind of machinery was he using, Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Building construction machinery for loading. I don't know what the correct name is, but these are large machines. I don't know the exact name of this type of machine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, on the 14th did you see any heavy machinery operating?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. They arrived on the 14th after I had been to Bratunac and come back to Kravica. And then our civilian municipal authorities recruited -- or rather, engaged the civilian protection and the utilities company. And a team arrived in Kravica on that day, the 14th. A group arrived. We didn't do anything on that day. And on the following day, the Saturday, they began loading and burying -- or rather, evacuating the corpses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, talking about these corpses. When you were there on the 14th in the morning, tell us about these dead bodies you have seen, these corpses. How many were there?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I can't say exactly how many there were. I can give you my own estimation, but there were quite a few corpses in both warehouses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So you looked inside the warehouses?
