utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you remember having given the number of 500 when you talked to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the number I mentioned, but I think at the time this was just a rough estimate. I cannot be precise. I cannot be sure whether it was 500, more, or less. I truly don't know the precise number.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, how many members does the Bratunac Brigade have?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: How many did they have?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So you are claiming you know every member of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. He never claimed that. How do you get from not knowing how many to knowing who they are? It's just -- there's a great leap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, during the direct examination the witness said that he used to be in the Bratunac Brigade, he knows many people in that brigade. So that's why the Prosecution asked this question in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree, Mr. President. But he says: "So you are claiming you know every member?" He never claimed that he knew every member. There is a distinction; he knows many, but not every. I don't want him to be misleading -- confusing the witness for the purposes of trying to set him into a trap. I know where he's going and I don't have a problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi, maybe you should rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Earlier today you said that you were sure that the executioners weren't members of the Bratunac Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I'm convinced that they were not, and I can support this by the fact that I had been physically attacked by those people and almost killed. As for my statement with respect to knowing the brigade, it's a fact that I know many men. I can't say that each and every member of the brigade knew me, but I'm sure that many of them knew me. 95 per cent of them knew me, in view of my activities before the war and my activities while I was a member of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, but there could have been members of the Bratunac Brigade which you did not know present on that morning. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There might have been some men I didn't know, but I am sure that there were very few who did not know me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you about the next issue. You said you went to the civilian authorities and basically informed them about what you have seen. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And I believe you said that Mr. Simic was there and that Mr. Deronjic came later?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Do you remember telling the investigators that Mr. Deronjic wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I remember I said Deronjic wasn't there when I arrived, but it's a fact that while I was in the office of the president of the Executive Board, Deronjic entered the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Well, that's not what you said to the investigators. You were asked a clear question, and I can --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If the counsel wants.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now we're having testimony from counsel. If he wants to point to a page, ask him: "Was this question asked? Did you give this answer?" I don't have a problem, but I don't want any testimony from counsel. If he can help us out here so we can also locate what question was posed, what answer was given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I can certainly refer him to the B/C/S statement. Perhaps he could be provided with a version. Your Honours, it's -- in the English version on page 34, line 9 to 19. And hopefully Your Honours will be provided with a witness statement as well if you want that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we could just put that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Certainly we can do that. Page 34, the English version. And the B/C/S version would be page 30, about from line 29 onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So the English version -- I'm starting from page -- from line 8. And in the B/C/S version, it's page 30, line about 28. You were asked: "What other members of leadership were there that you told this to?" And your answer was: "And president of the local government Davidovic. "Q. What was his exact title?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: President of the municipal government, president of the executive council.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Okay. And anyone else there?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Was Miroslav Deronjic there?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No." And it goes on. "Q. In fact, what was his position at this time?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. He had no position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Were you the member of the SDS party?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes." And so on and so on. Do you see anything in here saying that he came in later?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't see it here, but it is a fact that he came, and this is why I wish to add to what is stated here that I found in the office of the Executive Board the president of the municipality. We stayed there talking. I informed about this, and then Deronjic came later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, afterwards you testified that you went back to Kravica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: In fact, you went back to the crime scene?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I went to Kravica, because civilian authority said that civilian protection would come there after me -- or rather, the team in charge of sanitisation measures and the retrieval of corpses. So as a managing director of the co-op, I was duty-bound to contribute to that effort, to be there, and that was the reason why I went back there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So you went back is there to the warehouse where you have seen the executions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: A scene you have described to the investigators as "genocide," "horrible," "ugly."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, well -- now we're getting into whether this man thought this was genocide. And I take it that this is going to be part of their argument, since Mr. -- this gentleman, who they're trying to impeach, thought it was genocide, then obviously a genocide had occurred. I do object to this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, what other words to you suggest they shall use? Mass killings?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to know what the relevancy of this line of questioning is. He has described an event. The Prosecution have stood up during their case saying that all Serbs deny that this is going on. Now you have somebody coming in here who reported it immediately and told the Prosecution and is telling the Court without any protective measures so that the entire world knows what he saw on that particular day. So I don't know what the purpose is of having him go back and describe what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, Mr. Karnavas. The question is that: "A scene you have described to the investigators as 'genocide,' 'horrible,' 'ugly.'" If you do not agree with this -- what the Prosecution said, you may ask the Prosecution to find out where it is in the transcript or in the statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My question is to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But if the witness really said that, well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no objection, Your Honour. We brought the witness here, not the Prosecution. We readily admit that he saw atrocities occur. But I guess my question is: He testified to that on direct, what is the relevancy at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Waespi --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I can explain, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you find that statement made by this witness on that very issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: It's in the English version on page 30, line 27 to 30. And in the B/C/S version it must be around page 26. Perhaps if it could be placed on the ELMO. And the question I have is: If it was so horrible and if the witness even said he was threatened, physically attacked, why he would go back on his free will to that scene. That's my question I would like to get an answer from this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Then I withdraw my objection. I do not have a problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Nikolic, you just heard what I said. I quoted you, your words. And I remind you that you told us you were physically attacked. And now you are going back to that scene which you have seen --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I did not immediately go back. I spent a certain period of time in town. I also went to my administrative building. I consulted some people there. And then after I received the news from the municipality that the team for sanitation measures were headed there, only after that did I go there myself. And as I have described in the beginning, at that Kravica site we had a production going on. We had cattle there. We had some people there who worked at the site. So my task was to take care of these people and to see what was to be done with them. So all of these are the reasons why I was concerned and why I went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So you have seen these bodies. You don't know the number. You told us -- you told the investigators 500. It doesn't matter. Using your words, "genocide" and so on, "horrible." The only thing you are concerned about is that your business is operating well. Is that what you are saying today?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. No. The civilian authorities at the municipality told me that the team headed to Kravica was getting ready. So it wasn't half an hour that passed, but rather three or four hours passed. I wasn't alone to go there. The entire team went there. And I was among the people who went. I didn't go to Bratunac just to report what had happened and then immediate go back. I am telling you that quite a lot of time passed between these two events, several hours. So I wasn't alone who went back; the entire team went back, and I was on that team. (redacted), (redacted), Nikolic, the people working in the utilities went back, and I was among them. I didn't say that I was only concerned with the cattle, and that was the only reason I went back there. That's not true. I said among other things, there was also that aspect. After all we had people from the co-op at the site and we needed to help them to enable them to go back to their homes. So a period of time passed between my arrival in Bratunac, the departure of the sanitisation team, and my return back there. I didn't go back there alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me just finish that part. How many executioners were there?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: As I have already said there were four or five people in camouflage uniforms there. I saw a group of people. They were executing. That's all I saw as I was entering the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, let me turn to another subject briefly. You told us that you have seen buses with children, I believe, and women on the way to Kladanj. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The buses with children or the buses headed towards Kladanj I saw on the 12th. I didn't see whether there were just women and children there. That was on the 12th. And on the 13th, as I've said to you, there were buses leaving the area. I wasn't watching them alone. There were other people watching the buses as they were leaving town and heading towards Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we briefly could go into private session for one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just a couple more issues, Mr. Nikolic. Do you remember having seen Dragan Mirkovic at the Bratunac Brigade in the days after the fall of Srebrenica, together with Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No. I saw Dragan Mirkovic in Kravica when he came with the task to clean up the terrain, together with a team including Ljupko Ilic and the other people. So we stayed there on Saturday and Sunday performing those tasks. I never saw him at the brigade. I couldn't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So if a witness said that, that would not be correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So if a witness would have said that, that would not be correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Then it's a lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Okay. Let me perhaps finish and, in fact, following up what you just said, your last words about untruths. We heard today that you never mentioned Momir Nikolic as being together with you going to Potocari on the 13th. And I believe you gave your explanations about that. Now, you were extremely explicit when you talked to the investigators about telling the truth. And in fact, that's what you repeated today, that you came here to tell the whole story. And let me quote what you told the investigators when you met with them in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Perhaps if it could be put on the ELMO. Page 3, English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And for you, Mr. Nikolic, it's page 3, lines 26 to 27. And I would just like to quote what it says. "I came following this summons, not to defend myself but to speak the truth about the events that took place in the area of Bratunac and Srebrenica." And you end with an equally emphatic statement. Last page of the English version, page 41, lines 3 to 6. And the B/C/S version page 37, lines I believe also 3 to 6. After being asked about Momir Nikolic and not responding anything you said, and I quote: "And nobody had ever asked me any questions about what happened in Srebrenica in 1995. And I was very much surprised that I was summoned to come here as a suspect. And everything I said is the truth about," and then unintelligible word,"and that's why what I told you is the absolute truth about the events." In fact, also when you talked to the police in Bratunac way after Momir Nikolic pleaded guilty, you stuck to the story that you never heard anything about being accompanied by Momir Nikolic and indeed Mr. Vasovic, you never mentioned him in your statement to the Bratunac police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I don't have the statement I gave to the police. However, as for Momir Nikolic, I've already said what I needed to say. And I apologise to the Prosecution. I said that our town is a small one and that I had contact with him before going to Banja Luka. We talked, and he insisted that I do not mention his name with respect to the trip to Potocari. In view of his insistence and in view of the fact that nobody even asked me whether I went there with Momir, they just asked me whether I went there myself, so I corrected my testimony today with respect to that. And I stated that Momir Nikolic had gone with me to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me give you then this testimony -- this witness statement you gave to the Bratunac police. It dates 26 August 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown the statement, and we have an English translation which could be placed on to the ELMO. And I'm reading from the last paragraph of the first page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And in your B/C/S version it's -- in the middle it starts: "Nakon toga..." Let me read out what the English version says: "After that I was cautioned that pursuant to article 219, item 2 of the ZKP of Republika Srpska, he did not have to answer the questions of the authorised person, except giving his personal details. After being told what his position was and what his rights as a witness, according to article 150 of the ZKP of Republika Srpska where he was warned that he had to speak the truth, that he should not keep secrets, and that false testifying was a criminal act." Again, you have not complied with that, you have not told the truth. You were specifically asked about Momir Nikolic. Let's turn to the last page, page 5, English version. And in your version, it's almost the last paragraph starts with: "Ostala pitanja..." In English it says: "I don't know the persons which are mentioned in the statements of Momir Nikolic, and in other documents, and I cannot talk about that." So you were specifically referred to Momir Nikolic, and you choose not to answer truthfully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the witness is going to answer this question, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I want to note my strong objection on this one, because this is clearly inappropriate. There is nothing to suggest that he was asked a question about Momir Nikolic in Potocari. And I think if we read what's being said, it's being taken way out of context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, let's hear what the witness is going to tell us. We could read this paragraph by ourselves.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other questions where I say that the rest of the details concerning Srebrenica is something that I was not familiar with, because there were no reasons for me to know the details of the operation or specific parts of the action. I don't know the persons which are mentioned in the statements of Momir Nikolic and other documents, and I cannot talk about that. And who -- if you follow the testimony of Momir Nikolic, then you will know that he spoke specifically about people he had seen in Kravica whom he considers as having taken part in the killing of Muslims in Kravica. I said that I knew nothing about this and I didn't want to state anything further. The person questioning me did not insist on this aspect. So what is stated here is true. None of it is not true. I didn't know anything about Srebrenica, any military aspects, because I was not a member of the brigade and I did not participate in those events. As for what Momir Nikolic said about the events in Kravica, I didn't want to give any comments regarding that. I didn't want to state anything. So this statement I gave to the police is what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-direct? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. And I'll keep it brief. I'll keep it brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Since we have the statements there and since the insinuation has been that you were protecting Miroslav Deronjic or failed to mention him, could you please look at your statement, and in fact I have it marked for you the statement that you gave. And we can put on the ELMO page 3. We can put on the ELMO page 3, and I've even marked the area or I can read it into the record. Page 3 in the English version towards the bottom. You state, and I'll just read. It says: "I returned in my car to Bratunac and went to the municipal building. There I found assembly president Ljubisav Simic, executive committee chairman" - it's a misspelling of the first name - "Davidovic, and commissioner Miroslav Deronjic." So when you spoke to the police on 26 August 2003, it would appear that you mentioned Deronjic as being one of the individuals that you saw when you went there to report what you had witnessed in Kravica on the morning of July 14th, 1995. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, a couple of matters. You indicated, you indicated -- we won't need that anymore, so you can put the documents down. I'll be very brief. You indicated what you saw at the Kravica warehouse on the morning of July 14th, 1995. Are you fabricating this? Are you making this up, that there were Serb soldiers executing Muslims at that period of time in that warehouse on that morning when you went there? Is this a lie on your part?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I think it would be absurd for me to make something like this up. Why would I make it up?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, had you seen, sir, had you seen buses and trucks in Kravica? Okay. And I'm talking about by the school or by the supermarket, as has been suggested. If you had seen those trucks with men in them or those buses with men in them, would there be any reason for you to conceal that fact, in light of the fact that you went to the municipal authorities on the morning of the 14th to report the executions that you had seen. And then when called upon by the Prosecution to give a statement, you again repeated what you had seen? Is there any reason why you would conceal those facts?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There wouldn't be any reason, and I didn't conceal them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you indicated -- the question was posed to you whether you knew every member of the Bratunac Brigade and how could you be sure that the individuals there were not from the Bratunac Brigade. And I just want to make sure that I understand the reasoning behind your assertion that they were not from Bratunac -- from the Bratunac Brigade. And if I understand you correctly, what you're suggesting is in light of your position in the community and the fact that people knew you, you find it difficult to believe that somebody from the Bratunac Brigade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm entitled to finish my question for the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I don't know, is he cross-examining his own witness now by leading that? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My learned colleague obviously does not know redirect examination. I'm entitled to put a predicate before the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm more that happy to give him instructions later after the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, but you are asking a leading question. You're putting the answers in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The first matter is I believe the witness has already mentioned that issue in your direct examination and also cross-examined by the Prosecution. If there is still certain points you are not clear on, you may raise some questions concerning that particular question rather than repeat your question again and again by putting your answers in your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I wasn't quite sure that the point had been crystal clear in the record. I'll rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please explain to us why it is that you think that those individuals were not from the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I will repeat once more that when I entered Kravica and arrived at the warehouse, I saw the scene that I have described. The incident that occurred after I reacted to what was going on there and to the killings that had been committed there was that actually I had been physically attacked and was almost killed. I think that some other witnesses who were in the compound have made similar statements. My conclusion and my assertion that these men could not have been members of the Bratunac Brigade follows from the fact that for many years I had been the principal of the school, the president of the Alliance of Socialists, that I had been deputy commander of the brigade for the defence of the village of Kravica. There were very few people who didn't know me. Of course, I knew many members of the brigade, but I cannot say that I knew each and every one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the Prosecution has insinuated -- in fact, they have come out and directly accused you of being dishonest, untruthful, with the Prosecution in -- when you gave your statement because you failed to mention the fact that Momir Nikolic was with you on the morning of the 13th. Were you aware that Momir Nikolic was untruthful to the Prosecutor when he testified and that he was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I don't see the point in that, and certainly not in re-direct why he's pursuing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The point is it goes to motive. The point is Momir Nikolic gave a statement before this gentleman, and obviously now Momir Nikolic wanted to cover his tracks. So now Momir Nikolic goes to somebody that he knows is about to be -- to give a statement, and now he's telling this individual to keep his name out of the picture. That's the point I'm trying to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I believe that matter is quite clear. I don't think you need to ask this question again. And by the way, Momir Nikolic is not on trial in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He may not be on trial, Your Honour, but the Prosecution in their brief, the 98 bis brief has embraced Momir Nikolic as being a truthful and honest witness. They're relying on him, their star witness, in trying to implicate and convict my client. Therefore, Momir Nikolic's credibility is in doubt throughout this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt. But it's getting late in the day. If we can put an end to the antics and the argument, especially in front of the witness. If this is necessary, if it can be done outside the presence of the witness. We can all hash out what the Prosecution said about Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour. I was merely trying to assist the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope so. I really hope so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Argibay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: I do have one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. You remember you told us that this man -- the killers, let's say, were in uniform.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Although you couldn't see their faces. But did they have any insignias, characteristical pieces of -- a belt or a bandanna or something like that?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: This was the usual sort of camouflage uniform with the belts worn by the Army of Republika Srpska. There were no special characteristics on this uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Insignias?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't notice any insignia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Judge Vassylenko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: You testified that since long time you knew Momir Nikolic and Vidoje Blagojevic. And may I ask you to provide the Bench with any information as to relationship between Momir Nikolic and Colonel Blagojevic as members of the Bratunac Brigade or as -- in, let us say, as private persons.

utterances.speaker: JOVAN NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I was not a member of the brigade when Vidoje Blagojevic was the commander, so I cannot say anything about the relations between Momir and Vidoje. I already had an opinion about Momir, which may or may not be correct. As for Vidoje Blagojevic, the people in the town and in our municipality generally thought that he was a good and honourable man. And that was my impression of him when I met him. To be true, I didn't have much in common with Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Hvala. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judges' questions, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Waespi?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. The usher will show you out of the room. And all of us wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, what shall we do at this stage? Mr. Karnavas, I'm seeking your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm always willing to assist, Your Honour, when I can. I was prepared to call the next witness; however, Mr. Waespi and I -- well, Mr. Waespi, who is also doing the cross-examination, suggested that we take the witness tomorrow, and I thought, you know, since he's asking for that courtesy, I didn't object to it. And since I don't think that that witness is going to be more than a session combined, you know -- you know, for both cross and direct. He's a little bit shorter than this gentleman, so I believe -- and since he's scheduled for tomorrow and I have no other witnesses after that, I conceded the point that we should have him tomorrow. Perhaps I overstepped my boundaries in agreeing to that. But I still maintain and believe that we will be able to handle the witness and have the Status Conference tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And are there any protective measures for tomorrow's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No protective measures. And as far as proofing notes, I don't believe that there are any. I mean, I met with the gentleman, I spoke to him, and he more or less states what he stated -- what I put in his summary, with one qualification. I will set out and type out some proofing notes anyway just to be on the safe side and have them faxed and e-mailed tonight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you are not forced to do that unless it's absolutely necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right very well. And then for the next week we have four. We understand Friday is off. At some point I will be taking advantage of the situation where we end slightly early to have another witness ready. We're still trying to get everybody with their passports, so it's going to take a little time. But we think we're going to get everything rolling, because we appreciate the time the Court has given us to put our case together, and we don't want to disappoint by having free time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, one witness for one day is a general principle, but we notice in the future that you might have, say, six hours witness for the direct examination, so we have to save some time for those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I fully agree with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And there's a procedural matter, a scheduling matter. I have to announce that next week we have to be in Courtroom II for the proceedings. I know there is a disadvantage for Courtroom II, especially for the public hearing. But in the other cases they need -- I was told that they need much space for the big model. So the hearing is adjourned. We'll resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 5.47 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 23rd day of April, 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 25
